Cloud Agents Just Got a Major Upgrade - by Brian Turcotte Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in Cloud Agents Just Got a Major Upgrade Kilo's Cloud Agents are now more personal, configurable, and connected. Brian Turcotte Jun 25, 2026 4 1 Share Cloud Agents let you run Kilo from anywhere without a local machine. Spin up an agent from the web or automate with webhooks, point it at a repo, and it works in an isolated container so you’re free to do anything else. The Kilo team recently implemented several updates that make the Cloud Agents workflow feel less like a bot running on your behalf, and more like a collaborator agent that does the heavy lifting for you. Your name on every commit Previously, when a Cloud Agent opened a PR, the commit history reflected that. Now, you can connect your personal Gi

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: See it all in action. Video

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Remote sessions. Enable remote mode in the CLI and your local sessions show up in the web dashboard next to your cloud sessions. Your machine handles the compute, but the session syncs in real time. Start something locally, check on it from your phone, hand it off to a cloud session when you close the laptop.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: PR status at a glance. When a Cloud Agent opens a PR, you can see its status right in the Kilo dashboard. No bouncing to GitHub to check whether CI passed or the branch is ready to merge. It shows up next to the session that created it.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Profiles that know your repo. Agent environment profiles now carry custom agents, skills, MCP servers, and slash commands, so a session boots with your modes and project skills already loaded. Set a default profile per repository. Point a session at a repo and it picks up the right environment automatically.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Your name on every commit. Connect your personal GitHub account and every commit and PR the agent opens is authored by you, with the Kilo bot as co-author. Your contribution graph reflects the work you directed. Code owners get pinged correctly. Reviewers know who was behind a change.
